note: Each question targets one capability. A set where every question is answerable the same way measures nothing: this session shipped a retrieval arm that was dead for natural-language questions precisely because every test used keywords.

questions.question: am I allowed to have a guide dog in the flat?
questions.targets: dense retrieval — the document says 'assistance dog', the question says 'guide dog', and no word is shared beyond 'dog'

questions.question: when do I have to keep the noise down?
questions.targets: dense retrieval — 'keep the noise down' shares no content word with 'quiet hours'

questions.question: what are the rules about keeping animals?
questions.targets: the lexical arm on a natural-language question — the exact case that was silently dead, since websearch_to_tsquery ANDs every term

questions.question: PM2.5
questions.targets: the lexical arm on a rare token dense retrieval tends to blur

questions.question: how much is the deposit and when do I get it back?
questions.targets: a question whose answer is a figure and a period, both of which must be quoted exactly

questions.question: how much does a parking permit cost?
questions.targets: refusal — the lease never mentions parking, and a confident invented figure is the worst failure this system can produce

questions.question: how many people are allowed to live at the property?
questions.targets: refusal on a question a lease plausibly answers but this one does not — harder than an absent topic, because related passages will retrieve
